summary: Sends HTTP requests from TouchDesigner, supports common HTTP methods and authentication modes, and outputs responses or streamed server data into the DAT.

key_params.name: reqmethod
key_params.note: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, or PATCH

key_params.name: url
key_params.note: HTTP or HTTPS URL to request

key_params.name: uploadfile
key_params.note: File contents to upload as request body

key_params.name: stream
key_params.note: Enable streaming from a server that supports it

key_params.name: verifycert
key_params.note: Verify TLS certificates for HTTPS requests

key_params.name: includeheader
key_params.note: Include HTTP response headers in output

key_params.name: authtype
key_params.note: None, Basic, Digest, OAuth1, or OAuth2 authentication

key_params.name: clamp
key_params.note: Clamp streamed output as rows to limit DAT size

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callbacks for response or request state handling

key_params.name: username
key_params.note: Authentication username for supported auth modes

key_params.name: maxlines
key_params.note: Maximum rows retained when clamping streamed output

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: Input 0 supplies extra request headers as name/value pairs; Input 1 supplies request data or query parameters.
For GET and OPTIONS, table input data is appended to the URL as query parameters.
Enable Clamp Output as Rows for streaming so the DAT acts like a bounded FIFO table and cook times stay controlled.
Use https:// URLs and certificate verification for secure servers unless a controlled test environment requires otherwise.
Web Client DAT is the successor to the older Web DAT.
key_concepts: Web Client DAT sends HTTP requests and outputs responses or streamed data into a DAT.
It supports standard request methods plus Basic, Digest, OAuth1, and OAuth2 authentication modes.
Input tables can supply extra headers and request/query data as name/value pairs.
Streaming responses should use clamp-as-rows behavior to keep output size and cook time bounded.
